question: What is a metaclass in Python and when would you actually use one?
title: Python Metaclasses
direct_answer: A metaclass is the class of a class — it controls how classes are created, just as a class controls how instances are created. type is Python's built-in metaclass: every class you define is an instance of type unless you specify otherwise. You use metaclasses to enforce interface contracts (ensure subclasses implement required methods), register classes automatically, add class-level validation, or implement DSL-style patterns like Django's ORM model system. In practice, most metaclass use cases are now covered by __init_subclass__ or class decorators, which are simpler.
interviewer_intent: Tests deep understanding of Python's object model. Senior candidates should know when metaclasses are warranted vs when simpler mechanisms suffice.

sections.title: The class of a class
sections.content:
In Python, everything is an object — including classes. A class is an instance of its metaclass. By default, that metaclass is type. When you write class Foo:, Python calls type('Foo', (object,), {'method': ...}) to build the class object.

A custom metaclass lets you intercept class creation. You do this by subclassing type and overriding __new__ (to customize the class object before it's returned) or __init__ (to do post-creation setup). You specify a metaclass with class Foo(metaclass=MyMeta).

Where metaclasses are genuinely useful:
- Abstract interface enforcement: ensure all subclasses implement required methods at class creation time, not at runtime when the method is called.
- Class registries: automatically register every subclass in a global dict, used in plugin systems and serialization frameworks.
- ORM magic: Django's Model metaclass reads your field definitions at class creation time and sets up SQL schema, manager descriptors, and related accessors.
- Singleton enforcement: prevent more than one instance by controlling __new__ or __call__ on the metaclass.

Modern alternatives that are usually simpler:
- __init_subclass__(cls): called whenever a class inherits from yours — cleaner than a metaclass for subclass registration and validation.
- Class decorators: applied to the class after creation, like @dataclass.
- ABCMeta (from abc): enforces abstractmethod contracts — effectively a metaclass you never need to write yourself.

sections.title: Metaclass patterns
Metaclass rules
items: type is the metaclass of all classes — every class is type(name, bases, ns)
Override __new__ in metaclass to modify the class object before creation
Most metaclass use cases → prefer __init_subclass__ or class decorators
Metaclass conflicts: only one metaclass allowed; use MRO or inherit from both
ABCMeta is a metaclass — you're already using metaclasses via abc.ABC

seo.metaTitle: Python Metaclasses Explained — When and How to Use Them
seo.metaDescription: Understand Python metaclasses: type, custom metaclass patterns, auto-registry, interface enforcement, and when to prefer __init_subclass__ instead.

speakable_v2.hook: A metaclass is the class's class — it controls how the class itself is built, the same way a class controls how instances are built.

beats.content: type is the metaclass of every class you've ever written. When you define a class, Python calls type(name, bases, namespace) to build it. A custom metaclass intercepts that call and lets you modify the class object at creation time.

items: Django's ORM: ModelBase metaclass reads field definitions and builds SQL schema descriptors
Plugin registries: every subclass automatically registered in a dict
Interface enforcement: check at class creation time, not first method call

beats.content: For most use cases, __init_subclass__ is cleaner. It's a hook on the base class that fires whenever a subclass is created — no metaclass boilerplate needed. ABCMeta (which you get via abc.ABC) already handles abstract method enforcement.

speakable_v2.cap: Practical rule: reach for __init_subclass__ first. Use a metaclass only when you need to transform the class namespace before the class object is built — which is rare outside of framework internals like Django's ORM.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Natural follow-up: __init_subclass__ pattern, or Python descriptors which are what Django ORM fields actually use.
